title: Recursion (intro)
learningObjectives: Explain recursion (intro) and use functions with clear scope and behaviour.

understand.concept: Recursion occurs when a function calls itself to solve a smaller version of a problem. A recursive function needs a base case that stops the calls and a recursive step that moves toward the base case. Deep recursion can exceed the call stack.
understand.whyItMatters: Recursion is useful for tree-like data and problems with naturally repeated structure. An iterative solution may be safer or clearer for simple repetition.
understand.analogy: Recursion is like solving a smaller copy of the same puzzle until reaching a simple case.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; function execution, scope, closures, and call stacks follow JavaScript runtime rules.

explain.narrative: The base case stops when value is zero or less. Each recursive call decreases the value toward that case.

examples.explanation: The base case stops when value is zero or less. Each recursive call decreases the value toward that case.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the function results described.

practise.guidedTask: Write a recursive sum function with a base case. Trace the calls for input 3 and compare with a loop.
practise.independentTask: Build a small reusable function example. Test inputs, scope boundaries, and any retained state or side effects.
hints: Keep functions focused and names descriptive.
Know whether a callback is synchronous or asynchronous.
Add a base case to every recursive function.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Recursion (intro)</title></head><body>
<script>function countdown(value){if(value<=0){console.log('Done');return;}console.log(value);countdown(value-1);}countdown(3);</script>
</body></html>

<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Recursion (intro)</title></head><body>

</body></html>

questions.prompt: What prevents a recursive function from calling itself forever?
questions.explanation: The base case ends recursion when the problem reaches its stopping condition.

questions.prompt: What makes a function easier to reason about?
options: Clear inputs, limited responsibilities, and known side effects
questions.answer: Clear inputs, limited responsibilities, and known side effects
questions.explanation: Explicit dependencies and controlled side effects improve clarity and testability.
